attributes.name: aveva_reference_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this berth in the AVEVA Marine Engineering system. Used for integration with port design, infrastructure planning, and engineering documentation. Links berth master data to detailed engineering models and drawings.

attributes.name: berth_number
attributes.description: The official berth number or code assigned by the port authority. This is the externally-known identifier used in vessel planning, NAVIS N4, TOPS Expert TOS, and port documentation.

attributes.name: berth_type
attributes.description: Classification of the berth based on the primary cargo or vessel type it serves. Container berths handle containerized cargo, bulk berths handle dry or liquid bulk commodities, RoRo (Roll-on Roll-off) berths serve vehicle carriers, tanker berths handle liquid cargo vessels, and cruise berths accommodate passenger vessels.

attributes.name: bollard_count
attributes.description: The total number of mooring bollards installed along this berth. Bollards are fixed posts to which vessel mooring lines are secured. The count and spacing of bollards determine the mooring capacity and configuration options.

attributes.name: bollard_swl_tonnes
attributes.description: The Safe Working Load (SWL) rating of the mooring bollards at this berth, measured in metric tonnes. SWL represents the maximum load that can be safely applied to a bollard during normal mooring operations. All bollards at a berth typically share the same SWL rating.

attributes.name: cfs_proximity_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has direct or immediate proximity to a CFS (Container Freight Station) for LCL (Less than Container Load) cargo consolidation and deconsolidation operations.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: The date when this berth was officially commissioned and became operational for vessel berthing. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, depreciation calculations, and capacity planning analysis.

attributes.name: fender_condition
attributes.description: The current physical condition of the fender system based on the most recent inspection. Condition ratings range from excellent (new or like-new) to critical (immediate replacement required). Sourced from inspection records in Maximo Asset Management.

attributes.name: fender_energy_absorption_kj
attributes.description: The total energy absorption capacity of the fender system, measured in kilojoules (kJ). This represents the maximum kinetic energy that the fender system can safely absorb during vessel berthing without damage.

attributes.name: fender_reaction_force_kn
attributes.description: The maximum reaction force that the fender system can exert on a berthing vessel, measured in kilonewtons (kN). This is a critical safety parameter for vessel berthing operations and is used in vessel planning to ensure compatibility.

attributes.name: fender_system_type
attributes.description: The type of fender system installed at this berth. Fenders absorb the kinetic energy of berthing vessels and protect both the vessel and the quay wall structure. Common types include pneumatic (air-filled rubber), foam-filled, buckling (energy-absorbing steel), cylindrical, cone, cell, arch, and unit fenders. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pneumatic|foam_filled|buckling|cylindrical|cone|cell|arch|unit — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth meets ISPS (International Ship and Port Facility Security) Code requirements. ISPS compliance is mandatory for berths handling international vessels and includes security fencing, access control, surveillance, and lighting.

attributes.name: last_dredging_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent dredging operation to maintain the required water depth alongside this berth. Dredging is performed periodically to remove sediment accumulation and maintain draft capacity. Sourced from dredging records.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent comprehensive structural and equipment inspection of this berth. Inspections cover quay wall integrity, fender condition, mooring equipment, and safety systems. Sourced from Maximo Asset Management inspection records.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: The geographic latitude coordinate of the berth center point in decimal degrees. Used for vessel navigation, VTS (Vessel Traffic Service) integration, and GIS-based port layout planning in AVEVA Marine Engineering.

attributes.name: length_m
attributes.description: The total usable length of the berth measured in meters along the quay wall. This is the maximum continuous length available for vessel mooring and determines the LOA (Length Overall) capacity.

attributes.name: loa_capacity_m
attributes.description: The maximum Length Overall (LOA) of a vessel that can be safely accommodated at this berth, measured in meters. This is a critical constraint for vessel planning and berth allocation in NAVIS N4 and TOPS Expert TOS.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: The geographic longitude coordinate of the berth center point in decimal degrees. Used for vessel navigation, VTS (Vessel Traffic Service) integration, and GIS-based port layout planning in AVEVA Marine Engineering.

attributes.name: max_draft_m
attributes.description: The maximum vessel draft (depth of the vessel below the waterline) that can be safely accommodated at this berth, measured in meters. This is constrained by the water depth alongside the berth and channel depth.

attributes.name: max_dwt_tonnes
attributes.description: The maximum Deadweight Tonnage (DWT) of a vessel that can be accommodated at this berth, measured in metric tonnes. DWT represents the total weight a vessel can safely carry including cargo, fuel, crew, and provisions.

attributes.name: mooring_fitting_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of mooring fitting types installed at this berth beyond bollards, such as hooks, rings, cleats, or quick-release hooks. Different vessel types and mooring configurations require different fitting types.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The common name or designation of the berth, often referencing location or purpose (e.g., Container Terminal North Berth 1, Bulk Cargo Berth A).

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next planned preventive maintenance activity for this berth. Preventive maintenance includes fender replacement, bollard inspection, quay wall repairs, and equipment servicing. Sourced from Maximo Asset Management maintenance plans.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the berth. Operational berths are available for vessel scheduling, under_maintenance berths are temporarily unavailable, out_of_service berths are closed for extended periods, planned berths are under construction, and decommissioned berths are permanently retired.

attributes.name: rail_connection_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has direct rail connection for intermodal cargo transfer. Rail connectivity is critical for inland container depots (ICD) and bulk cargo operations.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this berth record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this berth record was last modified. Updated whenever any attribute value changes. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit purposes.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, operational constraints, or historical information about this berth that do not fit into structured fields. Used by port operations and planning teams.

attributes.name: shore_crane_count
attributes.description: The number of shore-based cranes (STS - Ship-to-Shore cranes, QC - Quay Cranes, or MHC - Mobile Harbour Cranes) assigned to or available at this berth for cargo handling operations. Critical for container terminal berths and determines throughput capacity.

attributes.name: shore_power_available_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether shore power (cold ironing) is available at this berth. Shore power allows vessels to shut down auxiliary engines while berthed, reducing emissions and noise. Increasingly required for environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management, IMO MARPOL Annex VI

attributes.name: shore_power_capacity_kw
attributes.description: The total electrical power capacity available for shore power connection at this berth, measured in kilowatts (kW). Null if shore power is not available. Typical container vessel shore power requirements range from 1,000 to 10,000 kW.

attributes.name: tidal_constraint_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has operational constraints due to tidal conditions. True indicates that vessel movements (arrival, departure, or cargo operations) are restricted to specific tidal windows.

attributes.name: tidal_range_m
attributes.description: The average tidal range (difference between high tide and low tide) at this berth location, measured in meters. Tidal constraints impact vessel scheduling, particularly for vessels with drafts close to the maximum depth.

attributes.name: warehouse_proximity_flag

attributes.name: water_depth_alongside_m

attributes.name: centroid_latitude
attributes.description: Latitude coordinate of the zone geometric center in decimal degrees. Used for distance calculations, equipment dispatch optimization, and integration with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) for cargo location tracking.

attributes.name: centroid_longitude
attributes.description: Longitude coordinate of the zone geometric center in decimal degrees. Used for distance calculations, equipment dispatch optimization, and integration with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) for cargo location tracking.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the zone was officially opened and entered operational service. Used for asset age calculations, depreciation schedules, and infrastructure lifecycle planning in SAP PM (Plant Maintenance).

attributes.name: customs_controlled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is under customs authority control as a bonded area or free trade zone. True: customs-controlled area requiring special clearance procedures. False: non-bonded domestic area. Impacts cargo movement restrictions and documentation requirements in Port Community System (PCS).

attributes.name: design_capacity_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Target operational utilization percentage for the zone as designed by port planners. Typically 70-85% to allow operational flexibility. Used as benchmark for KPI reporting and capacity expansion trigger analysis. Expressed as percentage (e.g., 75.00 for 75%).

attributes.name: drainage_system_type
attributes.description: Stormwater management infrastructure type installed in the zone. Storm sewer for direct discharge, retention pond for controlled release, permeable pavement for infiltration, none for natural drainage. Critical for environmental compliance per MARPOL and local water quality regulations tracked in Environmental Monitoring System (EMS).
attributes.references: MARPOL Annex V - Marine Pollution Prevention

attributes.name: environmental_monitoring_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone has installed environmental sensors for air quality, noise, or emissions tracking. True: active monitoring integrated with Environmental Monitoring System (EMS). False: no environmental instrumentation. Required for zones near sensitive receptors or handling bulk materials.

attributes.name: fire_suppression_system
attributes.description: Fire protection infrastructure installed in the zone. Hydrant network for general fire response, foam system for flammable liquid storage, sprinkler for warehouse protection, none for open yard areas. Required for IMDG hazmat zones and insurance compliance.

attributes.name: ground_slot_capacity_teu
attributes.description: Number of Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU) ground slots available for container placement at single-stack height. Represents the base stacking capacity before vertical stacking. Used for yard utilization KPI calculations.

attributes.name: handling_equipment_type
attributes.description: Primary type of cargo handling equipment deployed in this zone. RTG (Rubber Tyred Gantry) for automated container yards, ASC (Automated Stacking Crane) for rail-mounted operations, reach stacker for flexible container handling, forklift for warehouse operations, mobile crane for heavy lift, none for passive storage areas. Determines operational capacity and throughput rates.

attributes.name: hazmat_approved_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is certified and equipped for storage and handling of dangerous goods per International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. True: approved for IMDG cargo with appropriate safety infrastructure. False: non-hazmat zone. Drives cargo acceptance rules in Terminal Operating System.
attributes.references: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal infrastructure inspection for safety, structural integrity, and regulatory compliance. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling in Maximo Asset Management and Port State Control (PSC) readiness.

attributes.name: last_resurfacing_date
attributes.description: Date when the zone pavement was last resurfaced or rehabilitated. Used to calculate pavement age, predict maintenance cycles, and schedule preventive maintenance in Maximo Asset Management system.

attributes.name: lease_status
attributes.description: Commercial arrangement governing zone usage rights. Port operated: directly managed by port authority. Leased terminal operator: long-term concession to terminal operator. Leased cargo owner: dedicated to specific shipper/consignee. Subleased: operator has subleased to third party. Vacant: available for lease. Drives revenue recognition and billing in SAP FI.

attributes.name: lighting_type
attributes.description: Type of illumination infrastructure installed in the zone for 24/7 operations. LED high mast for energy-efficient area lighting, halogen flood for legacy installations, none for daylight-only operations. Impacts operational hours, safety compliance, and energy consumption tracking in Environmental Management System (EMS).

attributes.name: maximum_stack_height
attributes.description: Maximum number of container tiers (vertical stacking levels) permitted in this zone based on pavement strength, equipment Safe Working Load (SWL), and operational safety requirements. Typically ranges from 3-6 tiers for yard operations.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory infrastructure inspection. Calculated based on regulatory requirements, pavement condition, and operational intensity. Triggers work order generation in Maximo for inspection planning.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the zone. Operational: actively in use for cargo handling. Maintenance: temporarily unavailable for scheduled or emergency maintenance. Closed: administratively closed but not decommissioned. Planned: approved for construction but not yet operational. Decommissioned: permanently removed from service.

attributes.name: paved_area_sqm
attributes.description: Surface area with hard pavement (concrete or asphalt) suitable for heavy equipment operations and container stacking in square meters (m²). Critical for determining operational capacity and maintenance planning.

attributes.name: pavement_condition_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of pavement structural integrity and surface condition. Excellent: no defects, full load capacity. Good: minor wear, full operational capacity. Fair: moderate deterioration, reduced heavy equipment operations. Poor: significant cracking/rutting, maintenance required. Critical: structural failure risk, immediate repair needed. Drives CAPEX maintenance planning.

attributes.name: rail_access_flag

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this terminal zone record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and regulatory compliance reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: record_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated or last updated this zone record. NAVIS N4 for TOS-managed zones, AVEVA Marine for engineering-designed zones, manual entry for ad-hoc additions, GIS import for spatial data loads, legacy migration for historical data conversion. Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Data Governance Framework - System of Record Standards

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: reefer_plug_count

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, temporary restrictions, or historical context not captured in structured fields. Used by terminal planners and operations managers for knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: security_level
attributes.description: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code security level assigned to the zone. Level 1: normal operations with minimum security measures. Level 2: heightened risk requiring additional security. Level 3: imminent threat requiring maximum protective measures. Drives access control and surveillance requirements.
attributes.references: ISPS Code - International Ship and Port Facility Security

attributes.name: total_area_sqm
attributes.description: Total surface area of the zone in square meters (m²). Includes paved, unpaved, and built-up areas. Used for capacity planning, lease calculations, and infrastructure investment analysis.

attributes.name: total_capacity_teu
attributes.description: Maximum theoretical container capacity in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU) when stacked to maximum allowable height. Calculated as ground_slot_capacity_teu × maximum_stack_height. Used for strategic capacity planning and terminal expansion analysis.

attributes.name: truck_access_flag

attributes.name: vessel_side_flag

attributes.name: weighbridge_available_flag

attributes.name: cycles_at_failure
attributes.description: Total cumulative operational cycles (e.g., crane lifts, RTG moves) of the asset at the time of failure. Used for cycle-based reliability and fatigue analysis.

attributes.name: days_since_last_pm
attributes.description: Number of days elapsed between the last preventive maintenance service and the failure event. Key metric for maintenance interval optimization.

attributes.name: detection_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the failure was first detected or reported, which may differ from the actual failure occurrence time.

attributes.name: downtime_hours
attributes.description: Total equipment downtime in hours from failure occurrence to return to service. Critical KPI for MTTR (Mean Time To Repair) and availability calculations.

attributes.name: environmental_impact_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the equipment failure resulted in environmental impact such as fluid spills, emissions, or other environmental incidents requiring reporting under MARPOL or ISO 14001.

attributes.name: estimated_repair_cost
attributes.description: Estimated cost of repair in local currency based on initial assessment. Used for budgeting, financial impact analysis, and CAPEX/OPEX planning.

attributes.name: failure_class
attributes.description: Primary classification of the failure type: mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, structural, software, or pneumatic. Enables targeted maintenance strategy and spare parts planning.

attributes.name: failure_datetime
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the equipment failure occurred. Critical for MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) calculation and downtime analysis.

attributes.name: failure_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the failure event, including symptoms observed, conditions at time of failure, and any unusual circumstances. Critical for root cause analysis and knowledge management.

attributes.name: failure_mode
attributes.description: Classification of how the equipment failed: complete breakdown, degraded performance, intermittent fault, safety shutdown, overload trip, or component wear. Used for failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA).

attributes.name: failure_recurrence_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this failure is a recurrence of a previously reported failure on the same asset or component. Used to identify chronic reliability issues.

attributes.name: failure_report_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier for the failure report, typically formatted as FR-YYYYMMDD or similar pattern for external reference and tracking.

attributes.name: failure_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the failure impact: critical (complete operational stoppage), major (significant capacity reduction), moderate (partial degradation), or minor (minimal impact).

attributes.name: immediate_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of immediate corrective or containment actions taken at the time of failure to mitigate safety risks, prevent further damage, or restore partial operations.

attributes.name: investigation_assigned_to
attributes.description: Reference to the maintenance engineer or reliability analyst assigned to investigate the root cause of the failure and complete the failure analysis.

attributes.name: investigation_completed_date
attributes.description: Date when the failure investigation and root cause analysis were completed. Used to track investigation cycle time and closure performance.

attributes.name: last_pm_date
attributes.description: Date of the last completed preventive maintenance service prior to the failure. Used to analyze correlation between maintenance intervals and failure occurrence.

attributes.name: load_at_failure_tonnes
attributes.description: The load being handled by the equipment in tonnes at the time of failure. Critical for overload analysis and SWL (Safe Working Load) compliance verification.

attributes.name: maintenance_status_at_failure
attributes.description: The preventive maintenance status of the asset at the time of failure: current (up to date), overdue, recently completed, in warranty, or out of warranty. Used to correlate failures with maintenance compliance.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the failure report record was last modified. Tracks updates during investigation and analysis phases.

attributes.name: operating_hours_at_failure
attributes.description: Total cumulative operating hours of the asset at the time of failure. Critical for age-based reliability analysis and MTBF calculation.

attributes.name: operational_impact_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the operational impact caused by the failure, including effects on vessel operations, cargo handling, berth availability, and terminal throughput.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority classification for the corrective maintenance work: emergency (immediate safety risk), urgent (critical operations impact), high, medium, or low. Drives work order scheduling and resource allocation.

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the failure report: draft, submitted, under investigation, analysis complete, or closed. Tracks the failure investigation and resolution workflow.

attributes.name: reported_by_role
attributes.description: The role or position of the person who reported the failure: operator, supervisor, maintenance technician, safety officer, or shift manager.

attributes.name: root_cause
attributes.description: Identified root cause of the failure after investigation, such as component fatigue, inadequate lubrication, operator error, design flaw, or environmental factors. May be populated after initial report during failure analysis.

attributes.name: safety_incident_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the equipment failure resulted in or was associated with a safety incident requiring OHS (Occupational Health and Safety) investigation or reporting.

attributes.name: swl_exceeded_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the Safe Working Load rating of the equipment was exceeded at the time of failure. Critical for safety compliance and liability assessment.

attributes.name: teu_throughput_loss
attributes.description: Estimated loss in container handling capacity measured in TEU due to the equipment failure. Used for productivity impact analysis and financial loss calculation.

attributes.name: warranty_claim_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the failure is eligible for warranty claim from the equipment manufacturer or supplier based on warranty terms and failure analysis.

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Description of weather conditions at the time of failure (e.g., heavy rain, high wind, extreme temperature) that may have contributed to or influenced the failure event.

products.name: inspection_record
products.description: Records all formal asset inspections conducted on port equipment, including statutory inspections (PSC, ISPS, national maritime authority), periodic safety inspections, pre-operational checks, and condition assessments. Captures inspection type, inspection date, inspector name and authority, inspection scope, findings summary, defects identified, defect severity (critical/major/minor), corrective actions required, pass/fail outcome, next inspection due date, and regulatory reference. Covers STS cranes, RTGs, ASCs, AGVs, MHC, forklifts, and port vehicles. Sourced from Maximo Inspection Records.

attributes.name: corrective_action_deadline

attributes.name: corrective_actions_required

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: critical_defects_count
attributes.description: Number of critical severity defects identified. Critical defects pose immediate safety risks or operational hazards requiring urgent corrective action.
attributes.references: ISO 55000 Asset Management, ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: defect_severity_highest
attributes.description: The highest severity level among all defects identified during the inspection. Used for prioritization and escalation decisions.
attributes.references: ISO 55000 Asset Management, ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: defects_identified_count
attributes.description: Total number of defects, non-conformances, or issues identified during the inspection. Used for trend analysis and asset reliability metrics.

attributes.name: findings_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of the inspection findings. Provides an overview of the asset condition, compliance status, and key observations made during the inspection.

attributes.name: inspection_cost
attributes.description: Total cost incurred for conducting the inspection, including inspector fees, equipment rental, and administrative expenses. Used for maintenance budget tracking and cost analysis.

attributes.name: inspection_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the inspection cost. Enables multi-currency financial reporting and analysis.

attributes.name: inspection_date
attributes.description: The date on which the inspection was conducted. Principal business event timestamp for the inspection activity.

attributes.name: inspection_end_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the inspection activity was completed. Used to calculate inspection duration and resource utilization.

attributes.name: inspection_frequency_days
attributes.description: The required interval in days between inspections for this asset type and inspection category. Driven by regulatory requirements, manufacturer recommendations, or internal policies.

attributes.name: inspection_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the inspection record. Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this inspection event for tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: inspection_outcome
attributes.description: Overall pass/fail result of the inspection. Indicates whether the asset meets the required standards and is fit for continued operation. Conditional pass indicates minor issues that must be addressed within a specified timeframe.

attributes.name: inspection_report_url
attributes.description: Link or file path to the detailed inspection report document. Provides access to supporting documentation, photographs, and detailed findings.

attributes.name: inspection_scope
attributes.description: Detailed description of the areas, systems, and components covered by the inspection. Defines the boundaries and extent of the inspection activity.

attributes.name: inspection_start_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the inspection activity commenced. Captures the precise start time for duration tracking and scheduling purposes.

attributes.name: inspection_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the inspection record. Tracks whether the inspection is scheduled, in progress, completed, cancelled, or overdue.

attributes.name: inspection_type
attributes.description: Classification of the inspection. Indicates the nature and purpose of the inspection: statutory (mandated by law), periodic safety (scheduled safety checks), pre-operational (before equipment use), condition assessment (asset health evaluation), Port State Control (PSC), International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS), load test, or Safe Working Load (SWL) verification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: statutory|periodic_safety|pre_operational|condition_assessment|psc|isps|load_test|swl_verification — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 55000 Asset Management, ISPS Code, SOLAS Convention

attributes.name: inspector_authority
attributes.description: The organization or regulatory body that the inspector represents. Examples include national maritime authority, Port State Control (PSC), International Maritime Organization (IMO), classification society, or internal maintenance department.
attributes.references: ISPS Code, SOLAS Convention, Port State Control

attributes.name: inspector_certification_number
attributes.description: Professional certification or license number of the inspector. Validates the inspectors qualifications and authority to conduct the inspection.
attributes.references: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety, ILO Maritime Labour Convention

attributes.name: load_test_performed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a physical load test was performed during the inspection. Load tests are required for cranes and lifting equipment to verify structural integrity and capacity.

attributes.name: load_test_weight
attributes.description: The weight in metric tonnes used during the load test. Typically set at a percentage above the Safe Working Load (SWL) to verify safety margins.

attributes.name: major_defects_count
attributes.description: Number of major severity defects identified. Major defects significantly impact asset performance or compliance but do not pose immediate danger.

attributes.name: minor_defects_count
attributes.description: Number of minor severity defects identified. Minor defects have limited impact on operations and can be addressed during routine maintenance.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this inspection record was last modified. Tracks the most recent update to the record for audit and version control purposes.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the next inspection of this asset must be conducted. Calculated based on inspection frequency requirements, regulatory mandates, and asset condition.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation of the specific regulation, standard, or code that mandates or governs this inspection. Examples include SOLAS Chapter V, ISPS Code Part A, national maritime safety regulations, or ISO standards.
attributes.references: ISPS Code, SOLAS Convention, IMO Regulations

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional comments, observations, or notes recorded by the inspector. Captures contextual information not covered by structured fields.

attributes.name: swl_rating_verified
attributes.description: The Safe Working Load (SWL) rating verified during the inspection, measured in metric tonnes. Critical for crane and lifting equipment inspections to ensure safe operational limits.

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Description of weather conditions during the inspection. Relevant for outdoor equipment inspections where weather may impact findings or inspection feasibility.

Integrates with Maximo Spare Parts Inventory and SAP MM Materials Management.

attributes.name: voyage_id

attributes.name: actual_arrival_time
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the train physically arrived at the port terminal rail facility. Recorded by terminal operations for performance measurement and billing.

attributes.name: actual_departure_time
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the train departed from the port terminal rail facility. Recorded for performance measurement, billing, and Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance.

attributes.name: appointment_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the truck appointment system booking if this rail visit is part of an integrated intermodal appointment. Links rail and truck operations.

attributes.name: billing_status
attributes.description: Current status of billing and invoicing for this rail visit. Tracks the financial lifecycle from charge calculation through payment.

attributes.name: completed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the rail visit was marked as completed, indicating all loading/unloading operations finished and the train departed. Used for performance measurement and Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance.

attributes.name: container_count_discharged
attributes.description: Total number of individual containers unloaded from the train during this visit, regardless of size. Used for operational tracking and billing.

attributes.name: container_count_loaded
attributes.description: Total number of individual containers loaded onto the train during this visit, regardless of size. Used for operational tracking and billing.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rail visit record was first created in the Terminal Operating System (TOS). Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: destination_location
attributes.description: Geographic destination point or Inland Container Depot (ICD) to which the train will proceed after departing the terminal. Used for supply chain visibility and intermodal coordination.

attributes.name: edi_message_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the EDI IFTMIN (Instruction Message for Transport) or other EDI message that initiated or updated this rail visit. Used for audit trail and system integration.

attributes.name: empty_wagon_count
attributes.description: Number of empty wagons in the train consist. Used for capacity planning and outbound loading operations.

attributes.name: estimated_arrival_time
attributes.description: Current estimated arrival time based on real-time tracking and updates from the rail operator. Updated as the train progresses toward the terminal.

attributes.name: estimated_departure_time
attributes.description: Current estimated departure time based on operational progress and remaining work. Updated throughout the visit as operations proceed.

attributes.name: hazmat_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the train is carrying any hazardous materials requiring special handling per International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. Triggers safety protocols and regulatory compliance procedures.
attributes.references: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rail visit record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization.

attributes.name: loaded_wagon_count
attributes.description: Number of wagons carrying containers or cargo upon arrival. Used for workload estimation and equipment planning.

attributes.name: operator_reference_number
attributes.description: Rail operator's internal reference or booking number for this train visit. Used for reconciliation and communication with the rail carrier.

attributes.name: origin_location
attributes.description: Geographic origin point or Inland Container Depot (ICD) from which the train departed. Used for supply chain visibility and intermodal coordination.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority assigned to the rail visit. Determines sequencing and resource allocation for loading and unloading operations.

attributes.name: reefer_container_count
attributes.description: Number of refrigerated containers on the train requiring power connection and temperature monitoring. Used for resource planning and power infrastructure allocation.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or exceptions related to this rail visit. Used for communication between terminal staff and rail operators.

attributes.name: scheduled_arrival_time
attributes.description: Planned date and time when the train is scheduled to arrive at the port terminal rail facility. Used for resource planning and berth allocation.

attributes.name: scheduled_departure_time
attributes.description: Planned date and time when the train is scheduled to depart from the port terminal rail facility after completing loading/unloading operations.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of rail service being provided. Unit train serves single customer/destination, manifest train carries mixed cargo, block train moves pre-assembled groups, local service provides switching.

attributes.name: teu_capacity
attributes.description: Total container capacity of the train expressed in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU). Standard measure for rail capacity planning and performance reporting.

attributes.name: teu_discharged
attributes.description: Actual number of TEU unloaded from the train during this visit. Used for productivity measurement and billing calculations.

attributes.name: teu_loaded
attributes.description: Actual number of TEU loaded on the train for this visit. Used for productivity measurement and billing calculations.

attributes.name: track_assignment
attributes.description: Identifier of the rail track or siding where the train is positioned for loading and unloading operations. Critical for yard management and equipment dispatch.

attributes.name: train_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned to the train by the rail operator. Used for tracking the physical train consist throughout its journey.

attributes.name: train_length_meters
attributes.description: Total physical length of the train consist in meters. Used for track capacity planning and safety compliance.

attributes.name: train_weight_tonnes
attributes.description: Total weight of the train including wagons and cargo in metric tonnes. Used for infrastructure load management and safety compliance.

attributes.name: visit_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the rail visit. Externally-known unique reference number assigned by the Terminal Operating System (TOS) for tracking and communication purposes.

attributes.name: visit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rail visit. Tracks the visit through scheduling, arrival, operations, and departure phases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|confirmed|arrived|in_progress|departed|completed|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: visit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rail visit based on operational purpose. Inbound brings containers to port, outbound removes containers, interchange involves both, shuttle provides regular scheduled service.

attributes.name: wagon_count
attributes.description: Total number of rail wagons (railcars) in the train consist. Used for capacity planning and operational resource allocation.

products.name: rail_wagon

attributes.name: rail_wagon_id

attributes.name: registration_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Rail wagon registration jurisdiction determines regulatory compliance, inspection authority, and cross-border operating rights. Port authorities and customs require verified country-of-registration fo

attributes.name: acquisition_cost
attributes.description: The original purchase or acquisition cost of the rail wagon in the base currency, used for asset valuation and depreciation.
attributes.references: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) - Asset Valuation

attributes.name: axle_count
attributes.description: The number of axles on the rail wagon. Affects weight distribution, track wear, and operational restrictions.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Technical Standards

attributes.name: bogie_type
attributes.description: The type or model of bogie (wheel assembly) fitted to the wagon, affecting ride quality, speed capability, and maintenance requirements.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Rolling Stock Standards

attributes.name: brake_system
attributes.description: The type of braking system installed on the wagon, critical for train composition and safety compliance.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Brake Standards

attributes.name: build_date
attributes.description: The specific date the rail wagon was completed and released from the manufacturing facility.

attributes.name: certification_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the wagon's operational certification expires and requires renewal.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Safety Standards

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: The date the rail wagon was first placed into operational service.

attributes.name: container_capacity_teu
attributes.description: The maximum container capacity of the wagon expressed in TEU. For example, a wagon that can carry two 20-foot containers or one 40-foot container would have a capacity of 2.0 TEU.
attributes.references: International Organization for Standardization (ISO 668) - Container Standards

attributes.name: coupling_type
attributes.description: The type of coupling mechanism used to connect the wagon to other rail vehicles, affecting interoperability with different rail systems.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Coupling Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rail wagon record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: deck_height_m
attributes.description: The height of the loading deck from rail level in meters. Critical for container loading operations and determining stacking feasibility.
attributes.references: Association of American Railroads (AAR) - Equipment Standards

attributes.name: double_stack_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon design allows for double-stacking of containers, typically applicable to well wagons.
attributes.references: Association of American Railroads (AAR) - Clearance Standards

attributes.name: edi_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon is configured for EDI messaging integration with inland logistics partners and terminal operating systems.

attributes.name: gps_tracking_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon is equipped with GPS tracking capability for real-time location monitoring.

attributes.name: gross_weight_limit_kg
attributes.description: The maximum total weight (tare weight plus payload) in kilograms that the wagon is permitted to operate at, considering track and bridge load limits.
attributes.references: Association of American Railroads (AAR) - Interchange Rules

attributes.name: hazmat_certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon is certified to transport hazardous materials according to IMDG Code standards.

attributes.name: height_m
attributes.description: The height of the rail wagon in meters from rail level to the highest point, used for clearance calculations and tunnel/bridge compatibility.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Loading Gauge Standards

attributes.name: insurance_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the current insurance policy for the wagon expires and requires renewal.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Insurance Standards

attributes.name: insurance_policy_number
attributes.description: The policy number of the insurance coverage for the rail wagon, used for claims and risk management.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Insurance Standards

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent safety or maintenance inspection performed on the wagon.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Maintenance Standards

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent maintenance activity performed on the wagon.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rail wagon record was most recently modified in the system.

attributes.name: lease_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the current lease agreement for the wagon expires, if applicable.

attributes.name: lease_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon is owned outright by the operator, leased from a third party, or chartered for specific operations.

attributes.name: length_overall_m
attributes.description: The total length of the rail wagon in meters from end to end, used for train composition planning and yard space allocation.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Dimensional Standards

attributes.name: manufacture_year
attributes.description: The year the rail wagon was manufactured, used for age-based maintenance planning and depreciation calculations.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: The name of the company that manufactured the rail wagon.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Equipment Standards

attributes.name: maximum_payload_kg
attributes.description: The maximum cargo weight in kilograms that the rail wagon is certified to carry safely. Critical for load planning and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Load Standards

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next mandatory inspection of the rail wagon.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Maintenance Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, or historical information about the wagon.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rail wagon indicating its availability for intermodal transport operations.

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: The legal name of the organization or entity that owns the rail wagon. May be a rail operator, leasing company, or port authority.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Registration Standards

attributes.name: refrigeration_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wagon is equipped to carry refrigerated containers with power supply connections.
attributes.references: International Organization for Standardization (ISO 1496) - Container Standards

attributes.name: registration_authority
attributes.description: The regulatory body or national authority that registered and certified the rail wagon for operation.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Registration Framework

attributes.name: registration_number
attributes.description: The official registration number issued by the registration authority, distinct from the wagon number and used for regulatory compliance tracking.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Registration Standards

attributes.name: residual_value
attributes.description: The estimated residual or salvage value of the wagon at the end of its useful life, used for depreciation calculations.
attributes.references: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) - Asset Valuation

attributes.name: rfid_tag_number
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the RFID tag attached to the wagon for automated tracking and identification in rail yards and terminals.

attributes.name: swl_rating_kg
attributes.description: The Safe Working Load rating in kilograms, representing the maximum load the wagon can handle under normal operating conditions including dynamic forces during transport.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - Cargo Securing Manual

attributes.name: tare_weight_kg
attributes.description: The empty weight of the rail wagon in kilograms, excluding any cargo or containers. Used for load planning and compliance with weight restrictions.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Technical Standards

attributes.name: wagon_number
attributes.description: The externally-known unique identification number assigned to the rail wagon by the owner or registration authority. This is the business identifier used in operational systems and documentation.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Wagon Numbering Standards

attributes.name: wagon_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rail wagon based on its structural design and intended cargo type. Flat wagons have a flat deck, well wagons have a recessed center for double-stacking containers, spine wagons have a central spine for container placement.
attributes.references: Association of American Railroads (AAR) - Equipment Standards

attributes.name: width_m
attributes.description: The width of the rail wagon in meters, important for clearance verification and loading gauge compliance.
attributes.references: International Union of Railways (UIC) - Loading Gauge Standards

products.name: truck_appointment
products.description: Transactional record for all intermodal capacity slot bookings including truck gate appointments, rail service reservations, and barge slot allocations, made through the Truck Appointment System (TAS), intermodal booking portal, or carrier EDI channels. SSOT for all intermodal capacity reservation and gate slot management across road, rail, and barge modes.

products.name: wagon_consist
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of a rail wagon to a specific train visit. It captures the train consist (the list of wagons forming a specific train) — a well-recognized business concept in rail freight operations. Each record links one rail wagon to one rail visit with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific visit assignment, including wagon position, load status, container count, and discharge sequencing.. Existence Justification: In rail freight operations, the train consist (the list of wagons forming a specific train) is a fundamental operational concept. A rail wagon participates in many train visits over its lifecycle, and each train visit consists of many wagons. Port terminals actively manage wagon manifests per visit, tracking position, load status, container count, seal numbers, and discharge sequencing for each wagon-visit combination. This is not an analytical correlation but an operational business process.

attributes.name: wagon_consist_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for this wagon-to-visit assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: rail_visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the rail visit record. Identifies which specific train visit this wagon assignment belongs to.

attributes.name: rail_wagon_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the rail wagon master record. Identifies which specific wagon is part of this train consist.

attributes.name: arrival_load_status
attributes.description: The load status of the wagon when the train arrived at the terminal. Distinguishes inbound vs outbound cargo handling.

attributes.name: assigned_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this wagon was assigned to this train visit in the Terminal Operating System.

attributes.name: consist_status
attributes.description: The operational status of this wagon assignment within the train visit lifecycle. Tracks progression from planning through completion.

attributes.name: container_count_on_wagon
attributes.description: The number of containers loaded on this specific wagon during this specific visit. Varies by visit based on cargo type and stacking configuration.

attributes.name: departure_load_status
attributes.description: The load status of the wagon when the train departed from the terminal. Tracks whether the wagon was loaded, unloaded, or remained unchanged.

attributes.name: discharge_sequence
attributes.description: The planned or actual sequence in which this wagon will be/was unloaded during this visit. May differ from wagon_position_on_train based on operational priorities.

attributes.name: hazmat_on_wagon
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this wagon is carrying hazardous materials during this visit. Affects positioning in consist and handling procedures.

attributes.name: load_status_at_visit
attributes.description: The load status of this specific wagon at the time of this visit. A wagon may arrive loaded and depart empty, or vice versa. This is visit-specific, not a wagon attribute.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes specific to this wagon on this visit (e.g., damage observed, special handling instructions, delays).

attributes.name: reefer_power_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this wagon requires reefer power connection during this visit (for refrigerated containers). Affects terminal resource allocation.

attributes.name: seal_number
attributes.description: The customs or security seal number applied to this wagon for this visit, if applicable. Used for cargo security and customs verification.

attributes.name: teu_on_wagon
attributes.description: The total TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units) loaded on this wagon for this visit. Used for capacity utilization reporting and billing.

attributes.name: unassigned_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this wagon was removed from this train visit (if applicable). Used for consist changes and operational adjustments.

attributes.name: wagon_position_on_train
attributes.description: The sequential position of this wagon in the train consist (1 = first wagon, 2 = second, etc.). Critical for operational planning, discharge sequencing, and safety (weight distribution, hazmat separation).

products.name: sla_profile
products.description: Single source of truth for Service Level Agreement definitions, targets, and measured performance outcomes for port community participants. Defines performance commitments including vessel turnaround time targets, container dwell time limits, gate processing time SLAs, documentation processing windows, and billing dispute resolution timeframes. Captures SLA tier name, metric type, target value, unit of measure, measurement window, breach threshold, and penalty/credit terms. Also stores all operational performance measurement records: measurement period, actual value, variance from target, breach flag, breach severity, remediation action taken, responsible party, and measurement timestamp. This product subsumes what was previously a separate sla_performance concept — both SLA definitions and their measured outcomes are managed here as a single SSOT. Assigned to participants via service agreements. Enables SLA reporting, penalty/credit calculation, performance trending, breach alerting, and continuous improvement tracking.

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: vessel_operations|container_handling|billing_tariffs|customs_clearance|gate_operations|yard_management|berth_allocation|marine_services|infrastructure|safety — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM - Case Category; NAVIS N4 TOS Domain Classification

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The communication channel through which the service request was originally lodged by the customer. Includes the Port Community System (PCS) portal, email, telephone, in-person at the port office, EDI message, or fax. Used for channel analytics and digital transformation reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: portal|email|phone|in_person|pcs|edi|fax — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Port Community System (PCS) - Stakeholder Messaging; Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM - Origin

attributes.name: closed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the service request was formally closed after resolution confirmation or customer acceptance. Distinct from resolved_timestamp — a case may be resolved but remain open pending customer confirmation before closure.
attributes.references: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM - Case Closed On

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording when this service request record was first created in the data platform. Distinct from lodgement_timestamp which captures the business event time. Used for data lineage and ETL audit trail.

attributes.name: crm_case_reference
attributes.description: The native case identifier from Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM, the system of record for service requests. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational CRM system for reconciliation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM - Case Entity; SAP S/4HANA Integration

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the dispute_amount field. Required for ports operating in multiple currencies or handling international billing disputes involving BAF, CAF, or foreign-currency THC charges.
